result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You are invited to book an eye check. It is called a diabetic eye screening.
It checks the back of your eyes. It looks for damage caused by diabetes. This damage is called (diabetic retinopathy).
At the check, drops will be put in your eyes. The drops will make your sight blurred for 4 to 6 hours.
This check does not find other eye problems.
It does not replace your normal eye test at an optician.

## What you need to do
1. Book your appointment by 15 January 2027. Call 01632 960 377.
2. Bring sunglasses if you have them.
3. Bring your glasses or contact lenses.
4. Bring a list of your medicines.
5. Do not drive until your sight is back to normal after the eye drops.

## Dates and medicines
- 15 January 2027: the last day to book your appointment.
- The letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Where will my eye check take place?
- How long will the check take?
- How will I get my results?
- When should I have my normal eye test at the optician?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*

problems.explanation_says: You are invited to book an eye check. It is called a diabetic eye screening.
problems.letter_says: This is a test that everyone with diabetes aged 12 and over is offered every year.
problems.why: The explanation leaves out that this screening is offered every year. That helps the patient see it as a regular yearly check, not a one-off, but it does not change what they need to do now.

The suggested questions don't add any new worries or claims.
